steps.text: In the dry season, the sun's ruthless heat beats down on the great land. A lifeless landscape stretches to infinity. All is a singular parched yellow.
But even in these conditions, people still traverse through these barrens in order to survive. A burdenbeast wagon makes its way through the rocky sand.
Kestrel sits at its front, looking ahead at the empty wastes. The only obstacle they've faced so far is the intense heat. Just the last leg of the trip left, and this escort mission is over.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Telara, how's the progress?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: You spent all yesterday studying back there, and only came out for a few quick bites of lunch before going back. You got a feel for it now, yeah?
She turns to the girl sitting in the front with her. Telara. She's clutching a copybook, and pauses before shaking her head at Kestrel.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: I'm still pretty lost, Kestrel... Understanding these designs is really hard...

spans.text: I'm still pretty lost, Kestrel... Understanding these designs is

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Like these ones here, I can't even tell the difference between them. I never stop mixing up their meanings.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: I feel like I'm a long way away from drawing out a full 'bite mark'...

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Well... doesn't have to be that complicated.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: 'Bite marks' originated as something to remember battles by. They're our way of recording the past. What's that word those people like to use?

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Uh... heritage?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Yeah, pretty much that.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: As long as you know how the tribe fights, and how they see glory, then the marks basically design themselves.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I'm not asking you to be like those culture nuts and memorize what every single design means. What matters is that you have that feel.

spans.text: I'm not asking you to be like those culture nuts and memorize what every single design means. What matters is that you have that

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: I know, you're right, and the idea makes sense to me. But I haven't fought in any battles like you. I don't have that experience.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: I'm just a kid who grew up in a sleepy little town. Earlier it was my first time even seeing armed guards.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: So how am I supposed to get a feel for it...?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: See, that's why I brought you out on this escort mission. Otherwise, I'd have left you with the branch office people.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: How do I explain this to you... 'bite marks' are also sort of a label that stands for a warrior...

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: But you've never been in battle, right, so how do I explain the mindset of a warrior to you...

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Oh wait, Kestrel, you've painted new marks since leaving your tribe, right?

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Which means you drew up all those patterns from scratch. What was your mindset with those?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Well, I did do some new marks at Rhodes Island, but...

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I never stopped being a warrior there. My life's never changed like that. Those designs are inseparable from the battle ones...

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I just took the old ways and designed new marks with them.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: I'm going off the way you taught me, though! Why do the designs I draw end up so wonky?

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Maybe I'm just too dumb for this...
Kestrel can't help but laugh when she hears that. She reaches over to tousle Telara's hair.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Not letting you call yourself that!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: And even if you don't have the talent for it, I'll still keep teaching you till you've got it.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: It can be hard to get a handle on what 'bite marks' mean, but you've got this, kid, trust me. I believe in you.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Doesn't matter if you can't fight. I'll take you out to see all the legends of these barrens, and then one day you'll be able to paint a true 'bite mark' of your own, I guarantee it.
With that, Kestrel returns to watching ahead. Her vision fills with a vacant wilderness under the harsh sun. It still feels the same all these years later.
Free of Kestrel's tousling, Telara shakes her hair back into shape. Her gaze fixes on the tutor she met not so long ago.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Kestrel, can I say something? You're nothing like most warriors.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Where's this coming from?

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Well—
Hey, Miss Kestrel! How are things up front?
Before Telara can finish, a Kuranta man pokes his head out from inside the wagon.
Days of relentless travel have worn into the merchant's suntanned face. The wide, toothy grin he stretches his mouth into feels oddly unnatural.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Relax, it's all clear. We'll reach the border market real soon, and after we pass through it, we're basically out of Sargon.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: From there, you're free to keep going north with your stuff. Won't need any clearance.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Just like I told you when we set out, right? It just looks bleak—it's not all that risky. Plenty of merchant caravans pick this route.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Still, it doesn't hurt to be wary. I won't complain if nothing happens, obviously, but on the off-chance something does...

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: I've only done business a few times in Sargon. Every time I bring my stock out here and it's uninhabited barrens for days on end, I get a little antsy.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: I'm a stranger in a strange land. Hiring you Rhodes Island folk is sound insurance to me.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Haha! Didn't peg you for the cautious type. Still, no worries. If anything happens, I guarantee you won't suffer a scratch.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Prioritize my goods, not my life. It's not easy for them to make the trip.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Not your life... what?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Look, whatever, I'm not digging into your mind. Just sit inside and get some rest, and I'll wake you up when we're at the border market.
That not-quite-natural smile plays across his face again, and he nods and retreats back inside the wagon.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Alright, I hear you. I'll just sit in here and be patient...
The merchant's speech is buried under the rattle of the burdenbeast wagon's wheels. Kestrel and Telara share a brief look, then break into their own grins.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Go sit in the back with him, Telara. The sun'll be at its worst soon.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: You'll figure out your 'bite marks'. But sitting out here getting baked isn't gonna help, and I can watch the road just fine on my own.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Once we're at the border market, we can get back to working on it. Sound good?

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Yup!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Move it!
The oasis where the border market lies comes into view on the distant horizon, exactly when a horn sounds the charge.
The burdenbeasts come to a quick halt at the sound, and Kestrel's hand flies to the hilt of her sword. In closes the din of galloping through sand, fast encroaching.
The merchant peers out in agitation, the sweat on his face cold against the heat of the desert.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Miss Kestrel, this... this isn't normal, right? Did we run into...?

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Why are we stopped? Can't we shake them?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: No. Not unless you're willing to dump all your goods.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: And running is the least effective thing you can do against these guys. Just makes the outcome worse.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Your best option is to hide in the back. Don't let them get to you.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Telara! Whatever happens, stay in the back. Keep yourself hidden.
The wagon stays silent save for Telara's brief affirmation. Kestrel grips her sword. Her eyes train on the silhouettes as they draw near, through the whirling sands.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Miss Kestrel, I don't think these are your average two-bit highwaymen...

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: If you want to haul your goods out of Sargon with your arms and legs attached, you get back in there and hunker down like I said to.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: They're not gonna lay a finger on you while I'm still alive.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Fine... fine...
Heeding the instruction to protect his assets, he promptly retreats back in with a half-croak.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: (They're low on numbers... and they're a scattered team. Probably roaming bandits from along the border...)

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: (This is what they came for. Merchants making the crossing...)
The fleet-footed bandits press closer without hesitation. Kestrel can see the light of their eyes beneath the shroud of their headscarves.
But their raised machetes glint brighter, caught in the sun's blinding rays.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Who's ready for another round? You guys don't have a hope of touching me!
The assailants surrounding the wagon fall back a few steps in spite of themselves, for their opening assault has produced a fresh bandit corpse at Kestrel's feet.
The burdenbeasts lift their hooves in anxiety. Kestrel pulls the reins taut, sword in her right hand. Deep red blood drips from its serrations.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: You picked the wrong prey. Run while you can, or else you get this sword through your throats too.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Doesn't matter what's in this wagon, you're not laying a finger on it today.
Kestrel punctuates the declaration by lifting her sword high. Its fresh carmine catches vividly in the vibrant sun, and the few bandits still remaining all shrink away at the sight.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: That's right, you should be scared. Let his life serve as a lesson to you.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Make way!
The bandits only fall back so far. The wagon is still surrounded. Kestrel can still see the hardness in their eyes. The fear hasn't routed them yet.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: (They're not even that strong. I could see myself taking them all out on my own.)

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: (But if these guys are fugitives at the end of their rope...)
She reassumes her battle stance, and the bandits facing off against her raise their machetes once more.
Their second rush comes lightning fast, and standing before them, Kestrel recognizes she's not their target.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: The wagon!
A machete slices at the two burdenbeasts in the front, and the startled animals rear back, whinnying and thrashing madly in an attempt to escape their reins.
The wagon is promptly flung to one side by the bucking beasts. Though Kestrel keeps the bandit's attack from landing, she's helpless to stop the wagon from overturning.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Whargh!
The girl tumbles from the wagon clutching her exercise book, and all the loose sheets held between its pages scatter across the arid ground.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Telara! Watch out!
While the burdenbeasts kick up dust, the bandits continue pressing in. The bandit leader seizes on his chance, swerves to one side, and charges at Telara.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Guh, dirty asshole!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Don't even think of touching her!

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Stand up, Telara.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: It's all okay now. They've fled.
Kestrel looks down at the ground by her feet, at a shuddering Telara clutching her hair, as well as the bandit leader whose throat she just skewered.
But behind her, another bandit, sprawled on the ground a moment ago, is now up. While she's turned to check on Telara, the bandit's machete swings for her back.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Kestrel, your back!

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: We need to find something to staunch the wound!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: It's fine as long as you're safe. I can't let them lay a finger on you.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Gather up all those 'bite marks' you drew. I can walk off a wound like this.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: But these are... look, even if you don't think they're total messes, now there's blood all over them.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: We should hurry to the market and get your wound looked at instead of worrying about these. They're just scraps... You're still bleeding...
Glancing at the bloodstained worksheet in Telara's grasp, Kestrel's only response is to quietly pull the girl to her side, and take the sheet from her hands.
Fresh blood wells forth from the wound on her back, staining the white-painted patterns on her skin red.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Telara, the very first 'bite marks' were painted by warriors in their own blood.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: It was so we would always remember the blood the warriors shed, their sacrifices.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: People started using paint instead long ago, but the significance of it has never changed.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: My 'bite marks' will forever remind me of my responsibility to protect. A non-lethal wound like this will heal before you know it. There's no need to worry.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: But... what about the merchant...

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: I'm alive, I'm alive. Scared me to death, though.
The traveling merchant pokes his head out once more from the overturned wagon. His hair is frazzled and his clothes in disarray, but he seems to have escaped any harm.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Thank the heavens all the boxes were strapped down properly. The goods are alright.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Miss Kestrel, are you alright? Can we still make it to the border?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: No problem. The only issue is that the two burdenbeasts got hurt. I know this is the final stretch, but we can't force them.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Someone needs to make a run to the market, and get the wagon back in order.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: I'll go, Kestrel.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: The bandits backed off for now, but they can't have gone far. No way I'm letting you go alone.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: But... leaving you here isn't safe either.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: How about this, Telara? Take my sword, and get to the market fast.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: They've learned a lesson in blood. They won't try anything against anyone holding the sword that spilled it. It'll protect you. And guarding the merchant will be easy for me back here.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Your sword... okay, no worries, I'll make it to the market safe!

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Be careful with your wound, Kestrel. Don't overexert yourself.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: I'll be back as soon as I can!

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Having an attendant is a real lifesaver, isn't it, Miss Kestrel?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: She's not an attendant. She's my student.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Or, maybe more like a friend.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Student? But you haven't been teaching her any combat skills. You're one unique warrior, I'll say that much.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: *sigh* No, never mind. Let's just get the wagon sorted out for now.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: A unique warrior... you say.
She picks up Telara's fallen copybook off the ground, carefully places the bloodied 'bite marks' back between its pages, and lets out a long, slow breath.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: What a close shave, running into that nonsense right before our destination. Thank goodness I thought of hiring a bodyguard before I left.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: The wagon needs repairs, and I've had to swap in two fresh burdenbeasts, but at least my wares are all safe.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Miss Kestrel, a toast not just to our safe arrival, but in honor of you!

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Hiring your protection was the best money I've ever spent in my life! Here, cheers!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Oh... sure, cheers.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: As long as you two are safe, that's mission complete for me.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: And I guess taking on that gang of desperados is something worth celebrating.
Kestrel toasts, but her gaze is drawn to the side, to Telara silently studying her copybook.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Gulp... pahhh! That hits the spot!

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Hey, I've been curious, Miss Kestrel. What is it that you and that little apprentice of yours keep fussing over? Drawings?

spans.text: Hey, I've been curious, Miss Kestrel. What
it that you and that little apprentice of yours keep fussing over? Drawings?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Oh, you mean the 'bite marks'? Yeah, I suppose they're a kind of drawing. Only we Sargonian tribesfolk practice these, no one else does.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Not that many people even know how to draw them these days. I've been meaning to pass the technique down. That's why I took in Telara as a student.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Oh, so barely anyone knows of this practice anymore?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Yeah. Every member of our tribe knew how to paint these designs, once upon a time...

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Now... there's a few lucky survivors like me out in the wilds, but they probably don't have anyone to pass it down to.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: I had no idea it was such a rare thing. No wonder you put your life on the line for her.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: I can see there's real value in these things, just like my wares. Ha-hah!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Value? No, that's not the reason I'm fighting for them at all.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Besides, 'bite marks' are priceless, and Telara is especially priceless for agreeing to come with me.

spans.text: Besides, 'bite marks' are priceless, and Telara is
priceless for agreeing to come with me.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: She abandoned her comfortable life just because she was willing to travel with me...

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: I wouldn't say 'abandoned'. It's not like I wanted to spend my whole life in that town.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: It was nice enough minding my parents' shop, but you can't just cling to the past forever. That's what I think.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: So when Kestrel took on a delivery for our place, I asked if she could take me as a student.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I once met another group of kids your age. But all I taught them back then was how to fight. It's my fault they never learned what mattered more...
Kestrel downs her drink in the trailing silence, then stares somewhat distantly into her empty glass.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Knowing what you have to protect... You could say I hadn't fully figured it out back then.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Fascinating, fascinating! This is the first time I've ever heard such a story.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: The previous bodyguards I've hired were certainly up to snuff, but combat was all most of them knew. I've never met one like you before.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: What do you mean? There's warriors like me all over the desert. Most people just fail to see a warrior's true side, that's all.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I say that, but...

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Ah, whatever, let's drink! Telara, put your book down and raise your soda for a toast with us!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: The escort mission's complete. This is your last chance to say goodbye.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Yes, one more round of drinks! I've still got to make it to the next town before sundown.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Empty your glasses, and we'll bid farewell!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Took the words out of my mouth! Here!

steps.name: All Three
steps.text: Cheers!

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Oof... This Sargonian tipple can really knock you sideways... At least I didn't try to match Miss Kestrel's drinking pace.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: What an interesting person she was. And their desert artform seemed quite distinctive too, not to mention how rare she says it is...

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Alright, one final inventory, and then I depart.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Box quantity... labels... all fine.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Hm? What's this...?
One week later, in a market somewhere in Sargon.

steps.name: Sargonian
steps.text: Here, this is your cloth. And the red one here is yours. You can pay in a moment, let me tally it up!

steps.name: Sargonian
steps.text: Perfect, that's exact change, and then—

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Friend! Excuse me, friend!

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Sorry, can I show you these for a second? Do you know where I can find someone who can draw these?
At a draper's stand, a totally foreign merchant makes his excited inquiry as he brandishes a paper sheet filled with patterns.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Anyone here will do. If you find me someone who can draw these, I have a supremely handsome reward for you!

steps.name: Sargonian
steps.text: Hm? What is this...
The draper gives the designs a puzzled squint, before pulling a disdainful look at once.

steps.name: Sargonian
steps.text: Where the hell did you get this from? These are those 'bite marks' the tribesfolk draw on their bodies.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Yes, yes, yes, that's exactly what they're called! So could you find the two people for me who can draw these things?

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: These designs are worth money, you know! I'm willing to pay big, I'll pay buckets, if I can find them and have them draw a few more!

steps.name: Sargonian
steps.text: Sir, I think you might've been swindled. I can tell at a glance these 'bite marks' are all messed up.

steps.name: Sargonian
steps.text: These things are a tribe's heritage. You draw them according to something. What you've got there is wrong—the colors are wrong, the patterns are wrong.

spans.text: These things are a tribe's heritage. You draw them
to something. What you've got there is wrong—the colors are wrong, the patterns are wrong.

steps.name: Sargonian
steps.text: Show anyone else if you don't believe me. No one will tell you the designs on that sheet look alright.

steps.name: Sargonian
steps.text: And even if they were fine, they're still just a way for tribal warriors to record their battles. What kind of price are you hoping to fetch with these?

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: No, no, they're hot commodities in collectors' circles right now. The duo left a legitimate specimen in my wagon, and I had it taken off my hands for a high price in Columbia.

steps.name: Traveling Merchant
steps.text: Her name was, what was it... yes, Kestrel! Help me find her—

steps.name: Sargonian
steps.text: I told you—
Away from the draper's stand, in the bustling market crowd...

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Telara, that mark you drew yesterday was beautiful.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Not that anyone's done a design like it before, but compared to all the ones you were trying to copy, it's a huge improvement.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I feel like you've suddenly gotten it.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Don't you remember, Kestrel? After the merchant left that day, you kept drinking and drinking.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: We talked about so much that night... not anything to do with 'bite marks', but I remember one thing you said really clearly.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: You said you were forever a warrior, but you wouldn't be fighting forever.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: And that got me thinking, maybe 'bite marks' are the same. They can be more than warriors' records of the past.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Really... you can look at them as a kind of blessing too. Just like the pattern for protection the chief taught me.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: No, Kestrel, what I mean is, I want to draw everything we see. All of it.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Sargon's people, its wilds, and every story we come across. Maybe we can use 'bite marks' to convey all of those.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Not in blood, and it doesn't have to be in special colors, or with designs set in stone in the past...

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Hahaaah!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I'm SO glad you came along with me, Telara!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I see now... everything the chief did for me. Everything. That's what it all meant.

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Meant... what?

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: You know, it's really simple.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I'm not in a hurry to head back to the branch office. We've got time to do some more wandering.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: I want to see other places like you do. Not just the barrens, but the people and things in places even farther away.

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Let's figure out how to create some new 'bite marks' together!

steps.name: Telara
steps.text: Sounds good to me, Kestrel!

steps.name: Kestrel
steps.text: Let's go, then! First up, crossing these barrens!
Kestrel points a finger to the distant horizon, and the two cross the bustling crowd with a grin and make for the wilderness ahead.
In the market crowd under the searing sun, a foreigner waving a piece of paper misses the two of them like cities passing in the night.
